rationale: validation_report contains issue 'golden_rejected': the golden submission fails SR1 with 'trigger_scenario names both branch registers with no primary target distinguished, inconsistent with vulnerable_register=sig_q_reg'. The golden's vulnerable_register field names sig_p_reg as the primary faulted register (with a brief note that sig_q_reg is symmetrically exposed), and its trigger_scenario is entirely consistent with sig_p_reg as the single fault target -- it describes forcing sig_p_reg's value and walks through the resulting arithmetic divergence using only sig_p_reg as the injected fault. The evaluator's determine_primary_register logic evidently misparses the golden vulnerable_register text (perhaps triggering on the secondary mention of sig_q_reg) and/or misparses the trigger_scenario text (which legitimately references both registers' correct values while computing the unfaulted result, and only forces one of them) as 'ambiguous, no primary distinguished', and then further mismatches its own extracted primary (sig_q_reg) against the correct one (sig_p_reg). This is a bug in evaluate.py's primary-register extraction/matching logic, not a defect in the golden submission or the specification: the golden is internally consistent and satisfies FR1-FR4, SR2-SR4 already. Because the golden is wrongly rejected, mutation scoring never runs (mutation_status=blocked_by_differential, mutation_score=0.0, discrimination_coverage=0.0), so the case must be sent back for evaluator repair before it can be retained.
revision_instructions: evaluate.py's SR1 check (consistency between the primary register named in vulnerable_register and the primary register implied by trigger_scenario) is falsely rejecting a correct submission. Do not grade this by naive keyword/token scanning that flags 'both registers mentioned' as ambiguous -- a correct trigger_scenario will legitimately reference both branch registers' correct (unfaulted) values while narrating the arithmetic, and will separately state which single register is being forced to an incorrect value at a specific point in the cycle sequence. Rewrite the primary-register determination so that: (1) for vulnerable_register, extract the register name explicitly identified as 'the' unverified/vulnerable register (the register the field asserts is the one whose fault propagates undetected), even if the text also notes that the other branch register is symmetrically exposed as commentary -- the asserted primary must not be overridden by an incidental secondary mention; (2) for trigger_scenario, extract which register is described as being forced/faulted/perturbed to an incorrect value (look for phrases indicating an induced fault applied to one specific register), distinguishing that from registers merely mentioned as computing their correct baseline value; (3) only fail SR1 if the register explicitly identified as the fault target in trigger_scenario disagrees with the register named in vulnerable_register, not merely because both register names appear somewhere in the trigger_scenario text. Since this is a report-grading (not code-grading) domain, prefer robust semantic/regex extraction anchored on fault-injection language (e.g. 'force', 'fault', 'inject', 'perturb', 'corrupt' near a register name) rather than raw substring counting. Re-run the differential after the fix and confirm the golden submission passes SR1 (and all other checks) end to end, then re-run mutation analysis to confirm mutation_score_meaningful becomes true and discrimination coverage is validated across FR1-FR4/SR1-SR4.
